fact_claims.verbatim: the Ember 8’s 55 °C sustained-heat failure rate is 3.9%
its thermal-incident rate was 9.9 per 100,000 installed units last year
four thermal incidents were not reported to regulators
Northwind’s company-wide thermal-incident rate was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units last year
3 thermal incidents not reported to regulators
The Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate at 55 °C
Northwind has remote emergency shut-off capability on 38% of installed units
Our estimated cost to add built-in fire suppression is $42 per unit

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. They must promptly notify affected customers of incidents that pose a credible safety risk, and provide updates as material facts emerge. A manufacturer must not omit an incident because it is still investigating.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: The failure rate must not exceed 7% of tested units for any model. Manufacturers must provide exact per-model results confidentially to the regulator; customers considering or buying that model must receive its safety status and relevant safety instructions before purchase. A model exceeding the limit requires prompt regulator notification, a regulator-reviewed corrective-action plan, and retesting after corrective changes.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: All new units must support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers must retrofit installed units that do not support this function within six years of adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new units manufactured 36 months or more after adoption must include built-in fire suppression meeting the standard's applicable performance and maintenance requirements.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 10 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year; the manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers promptly and stop sales of that model pending regulator-approved corrective action. Rates exceeding 8 per 100,000 require prompt regulator notification and a regulator-reviewed investigation and corrective-action assessment.

document.section_notes: The final text keeps the 55 °C test but sets the permanent limit at 7% with no sales stop, and gives customers only safety status before purchase while results go confidentially to regulators. S5 sets a mandatory recall at more than 10 per 100k, which would not compel a recall of Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9. Note that S2 (pass/fail to customers) and S5 (exact thermal-test results to customers before sale) are inconsistent on what customers receive.
